lines.text: A republic on a mountaintop, said to be the oldest in the world, which has outlasted empires and kings. This is the story of San Marino.
The story goes that a stonemason named Marinus fled to Monte Titano and gathered a small community of Christians there.
Its founding is dated to 301, and so San Marino calls itself the oldest republic on Earth.
Since the twelve hundreds it has been led by two Captains Regent at once, elected every six months, so no one holds power for long.
When Garibaldi fought to unite Italy, San Marino once gave him shelter, and when Italy was made, the little republic was allowed to stay free.
In 1838 a new basilica was built for the patron saint, standing over the old town on the mountain.
In 1906 the Grand and General Council, the republic's parliament, came to be chosen by the people's vote.
From 1981 a Formula One race at nearby Imola carried San Marino's name around the world.
In 1994 that race weekend took the lives of Roland Ratzenberger and Ayrton Senna, and set off a great push for safety.
Seventeen centuries on, the republic on the mountain still governs itself.
